verdict: Mid-America Apartment Communities collected $560M of rent and other property revenue, up 1%, and earned $86M while Core FFO — the REIT cash-profit measure — was $2.10 per share.

segments.name: Rental revenues
segments.note: Rent from apartment residents across the portfolio — $515M from the same-store portfolio and $40M from newer and other properties (10-Q disaggregation, rounded), including utility reimbursements billed to residents.

segments.name: Other property revenues
segments.note: Non-refundable fees, commissions and other property-level income.

opex.name: Depreciation & amortization
opex.note: Spreading the cost of the apartment buildings over their accounting lives — the big non-cash cost that makes REIT GAAP profit look small next to FFO.

takeaways.title: Core FFO met expectations
takeaways.text: Core FFO (non-GAAP) was $2.10 per diluted share, down from $2.16 a year ago, as MAA built occupancy through the quarter and kept expense growth disciplined; GAAP net income was $86M.

takeaways.title: Renewals are carrying pricing
takeaways.text: Renewing-resident lease pricing rose 5.3% year over year, up 80 basis points, with record retention and turnover of just 39.6%. Same-store blended lease growth was 0.4%, and October new-lease pricing turned positive year over year for the first time in 2026.

takeaways.title: Interest is the growing cost
takeaways.text: Interest expense rose to $55M from $46M a year ago on a higher debt balance and rate — a key reason MAA trimmed its full-year Core FFO guidance even as October pricing accelerated.

oneTimers: Results include a net $1M legal benefit: $2M of recoveries recorded in other non-operating income, partly offset by $1M (rounded) of real-estate joint-venture expense — see the 10-Q discussion of the $2.4M recovery and $1.5M expense in thousands.
otherDetail: Net other expense of $53M: interest expense of $55M and a $1M loss from a real-estate joint venture, partly offset by $3M of other non-operating income (including legal recoveries).
follow100Note: Depreciation takes $29.82 of every $100 — almost twice the $15.37 kept as GAAP profit. That is exactly why REIT investors watch FFO, which adds most depreciation back: Core FFO was $2.10 per share versus $0.72 of GAAP EPS.
footerNote: MAA is a REIT: the flow uses GAAP net income of $86M (consolidated, before $2M attributable to noncontrolling interests; $83M was available to common shareholders after preferred dividends). FFO and Core FFO are non-GAAP and appear in the KPIs and takeaways only. Cost of revenue is property operating expenses excluding depreciation ($144M of operating costs plus $78M of real-estate taxes and insurance, from the 10-Q, in $M rounded from thousands); revenue lines are the 10-Q disaggregation (rental $556M, other property $4M) footing to the $560M reported total.
